rules.what: Chisos Basin Campground (60 sites; most sites)
rules.rule: Reservable year-round on Recreation.gov; some sites 6 months ahead, others 2 weeks ahead. All sites require reservation (no first-come, first-served). Chisos Basin construction projects start spring 2026 for ~2 years; expect access disruptions (NPS).
rules.release_time: UNVERIFIED (not stated on NPS or Recreation.gov campground page; Seasons & Booking tab is JS-rendered and could not be read)

rules.rule: These sites are reservable up to 14 days (two weeks) in advance (rolling daily window); the remaining sites use the longer 6-month window.

rules.what: Backcountry permits (Chisos backpacking, primitive roadside, desert backpacking)
rules.rule: NPS (page updated 2026-07-20): a permit is required for ALL backcountry camping. Normally issued in person at Panther Junction 24h before first night (8:30 am-5:00 pm daily); some roadside + Chisos sites bookable online up to 180 days ahead on Recreation.gov (1-877-444-6777). BUT 'until further notice' (rain/road closures) ALL backcountry campsites are in-person only at Panther Junction; Chisos Mountains sites in-person only May 1-Oct 31. $10/night. Max 14 consecutive nights. Pre-booked Rec.gov permits cannot be changed by park staff.
rules.release_time: Online release time UNVERIFIED; in-person 8:30 am-5:00 pm
rules.tz: Park local (America/Chicago) for in-person hours; online release tz UNVERIFIED

winter.summary: Winter is Big Bend's main season (NPS: Oct-Apr). Nov-Apr all park campgrounds and the Chisos lodge are full every night; reservations required, no first-come camping. Mild and usually sunny, freezing spells possible, snow rare. Jan 1-Apr 15: 14-night park limit. Backcountry permits currently in person only at Panther Junction. Chisos Basin construction runs ~2 years from spring 2026.
notes: Primary visitor season October-April; Thanksgiving, Christmas-New Year, spring break and holiday weekends busiest (NPS advice-for-busy-times, page updated 2024-11-18).
Nov-Apr: Chisos Mountains Lodge and all developed campgrounds full every night; online reservations up to 6 months ahead, a limited number 14 days ahead; no first-come sites, no overflow/boondocking.
Rio Grande Village Campground open year-round, prime season Nov 1-Apr 30 (reduced to 25 sites May-Oct) - from NPS page excerpt; winter highs mid-70s to low 80s F.
Jan 1-Apr 15: limited to 14 total nights in the park (NPS camping page, updated 2026-07-20).

Backcountry: 'until further notice' all backcountry campsites in person only at Panther Junction (24h ahead); Chisos Mountains sites in person only May 1-Oct 31 (NPS bc_usepermits page, updated 2026-07-20).
Chisos Basin construction projects begin spring 2026 for ~2 years; expect access disruptions (NPS Chisos Basin campground page, updated 2026-01-30).
Winter-specific reservation/permit dates: none found on official pages.

rules.what: Upper Pines, Lower Pines, North Pines*, Wawona, Hodgdon Meadow campgrounds
rules.rule: Released 5 months ahead on the 15th of each month; each release covers arrivals from the 15th through the 14th of the following month (e.g. Jan 15 -> May 15-Jun 14 arrivals). *North Pines used a one-time early-access lottery for 2026; leftovers on normal dates.
Half of sites released 2 months ahead on the 15th (Jun 15, Jul 15, Aug 15 per NPS table); other half on a rolling 14-day window.

rules.what: Half Dome day-hike permits (cables up ~late May to mid-Oct)
rules.rule: Preseason lottery on Recreation.gov: apply Mar 1-Mar 31 (eastern time), 225 permits/day, results mid-April, up to 6 people/application, $10 non-refundable application fee + $10/person if awarded. Daily lottery: apply 2 days before the hike, midnight-4 pm Pacific, results that night. NPS page last updated 2025-06-03: 2027 dates/fees not re-confirmed.

winter.summary: Winter details NOT researched (UNVERIFIED). NPS says no advance reservations in 2026, including the Feb-March firefall period.
notes: NPS Feb 18 2026 release: Yosemite will not require advance reservations in 2026, including Feb-March firefall.

winter.summary: Zion is open year-round and winter is quiet but real: daytime ~30-60F. Canyon shuttles stop Nov 29-Dec 25 and again after Jan 2 until spring, so private vehicles can drive Zion Canyon Scenic Drive (parking limited; road can close when full); shuttles run Dec 26-Jan 2. Angels Landing still needs a permit and is dangerous when icy; the Dec-Feb seasonal lottery runs Oct 1-20. Watchman is open year-round; South and Lava Point close; Kolob Terrace/Lava Point roads typically closed fall-spring.
notes: Shuttle (2026-27 NPS schedule, page updated 2026-07-01): Oct 25-Nov 28 reduced hours; Nov 29-Dec 25 no service; Dec 26-Jan 2 service (8 am-4:30 pm); after Jan 2 no service until spring (typically March).

Private vehicles may drive the Scenic Drive only outside shuttle season (NPS: usually December-February); not during the Dec 26-Jan 2 holiday shuttle. If parking fills the NPS may temporarily close the road.

Angels Landing: permit required all times of year; winter hikes (Dec 1-Feb 28) via seasonal lottery Oct 1-20 (permits Oct 25) or day-before lottery; ice/snow may make the trail impassable (Rec.gov/NPS permit pages).
Watchman Campground open year-round, reservable 6 months ahead; South Campground and Lava Point close seasonally (NPS conditions page, updated 2026-09-16).

Kolob Terrace Road usually closed for months fall-spring (gate at Maloney Hill); Lava Point Road typically closed fall into spring; Kolob Canyons Road closes frequently in winter; Zion-Mt. Carmel Hwy kept open year-round but sometimes closes (snow/ice/rockfall).
Long-term closures: Hidden Canyon closed; Observation Point not reachable from Zion Canyon (East Rim rockfall). Winter daytime temps typically 30-60F.

rules.rule: Early-access lottery on Recreation.gov opens the 16th, closes the 1st at 5 pm MST, for start dates 4 months later (e.g. Jan 1 close -> May starts). Results the 2nd. Up to 750 winners get early time slots; everyone else gets access/public release 8 am MST on the 1st of the following month. rules.what: Reservation campgrounds (Apgar, Many Glacier, Fish Creek, Avalanche, St. Mary, Two Medicine, Sprague Creek; 8 of 13 campgrounds)
rules.rule: Sites become reservable on a rolling basis 6 months ahead of the stay date on Recreation.gov; a certain number of sites reservable 4 days ahead. All sites at these campgrounds require reservation. (NPS page updated 2026-07-09; Rec.gov Apgar/Many Glacier pages: 'Most sites have a 6-month booking window with a good handful having a 4-day booking window'.) Group sites: Apgar groups 6 months ahead (NPS FAQ, post-summer 2024); St. Mary group site was 1 year ahead per FAQ (not re-confirmed).
rules.release_time: UNVERIFIED (not stated on NPS or Rec.gov text; the generic Rec.gov article says most campgrounds go on sale 7am PT/8am MT/10am ET 'but not always')

rules.rule: Permit required for all overnight backcountry camping. ~70% of sites reservable in advance on Recreation.gov, ~30% walk-up (day before/day of, at a permit office). 2026: early-access lotteries - large groups (9-12, 5 reservations) applications Mar 1, 2026 12:00 am-11:59 pm MT; standard groups (1-8) applications Mar 15, 2026 12:00 am-11:59 pm MT (lottery winners notified Mar 17; may book Mar 21-Apr 30). $10 non-refundable lottery fee. General on-sale: May 1, 2026 at 8:00 MT through Sep 30, 2026 for remaining sites. Permit $10 + $7/person/night (May 1-Oct 31); free in winter (Nov 1-Apr 30). 2027 dates NOT yet published on the page (last updated 2026-02-23) - do not assume a repeat.
rules.release_time: Lottery 12:00 am-11:59 pm; general on-sale 8:00 am

rules.what: Vehicle reservations (Going-to-the-Sun Road) + Logan Pass shuttle
rules.rule: 2026: NO vehicle reservations required anywhere in the park (NPS, updated 2026-06-22). Instead: ticketed Logan Pass shuttle ($1/ticket, Rec.gov; part of tickets 60 days ahead rolling at 8 am MDT from May 2, 2026; rest at 7 pm MDT for next-day entry from Jun 30; shuttle Jul 1-Sep 7, 2026) and 3-hour limited parking at Logan Pass. 2027: NO official announcement found (NPS says operations are typically announced in spring) - status UNKNOWN; do not assume.
rules.release_time: Shuttle (2026 only): 8:00 am MDT (60-day) / 7:00 pm MDT (next-day)

winter.summary: Winter is for quiet snowshoeing/skiing, not driving: Going-to-the-Sun Road is plowed/open only from West Glacier to Lake McDonald Lodge (to Avalanche Creek until ~mid-Dec); alpine sections close ~third Monday of October. St. Mary/Logan Pass visitor centers closed; no in-park lodging. Apgar Loop B is free primitive first-come camping Nov 1-Mar 31. Winter wilderness permits (Nov 1-Apr 30) are free, issued by email at least 7 days ahead.
notes: GTSR open year-round West Glacier to Lake McDonald Lodge, weather permitting; unplowed section beyond is a popular ski/snowshoe route (NPS winter page - page last updated 2023-12-13, so re-check).

Alpine sections of GTSR typically close ~third Monday of October (NPS directions page excerpt); Nov-early Dec road open to Avalanche Creek, then closed at Lake McDonald Lodge from mid-December (NPS Nov/Dec page excerpt).
St. Mary and Logan Pass visitor centers closed; Apgar Visitor Center open weekends in winter per the 2023-dated page; no lodging in the park in winter.

Apgar Campground Loop B: primitive, first-come, no reservation needed, no charge from Nov 1 (open Nov 1-Mar 31 per reservation-campgrounds page, updated 2026-07-09); St. Mary partly open, no reservation in winter.

Winter wilderness permits Nov 1-Apr 30: free, by email request to glac_backcountry_permits@nps.gov at least 7 days before start; no permit office open (NPS page updated 2026-02-23). Note: the older winter page says in-person at Apgar up to 24h ahead - conflicting; use the newer page and confirm.
2026-27 winter-specific reservation dates beyond the above: none found.

rules.rule: Permits required year-round, booked on Recreation.gov (no trailhead self-registration, no same-day walk-up holds). High-elevation areas only reservable online ~mid-July to mid-October.
